title: Thai Veggie and Chickpea Curry
subtitle: Cook Once, Serve More!
description: Serve up more with our Feed A Crowd recipes! Using more hearty ingredients like filling carbs, proteins and veggies, you can satisfy extra hungry tummies or keep something for tomorrow’s lunch. If you’re on a 2-person plan, these recipes make 4 portions; on a 4-person plan, they make 8 portions.

steps.text: Cook rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put in a medium saucepan with 450ml water, cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins. Fluff the rice with a fork.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, thinly slice the onion. Halve the carrots lengthwise and thinly slice on an angle. Trim the beans and halve on an angle. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

Soften veggies: Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a large deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and garlic, stirring, for 3-4 mins until the onion is softened. Add the curry paste (see Feed A Crowd) and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant.

Simmer curry: Add the coconut milk, chickpeas and 250ml (1 cup) water to the veggies and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins. Add the beans, 1 tbs soy sauce and 2 tsp sugar and cook for 2 mins or until the beans are tender and the sauce is slightly thickened. Remove the pan from the heat.
Serve up: Taste the curry, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the rice and curry among bowls and enjoy!

Feed A Crowd: The curry paste contains chilli, so if you prefer less heat, adjust the amount to taste. Alternatively, if you like your curries hot, scatter with chopped fresh chilli or dried chilli flakes to serve.
